Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 30-Dec-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.Tech. (INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY) EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3123/ICT_3123 - SOFTWARE ENGINEERING  
  (MAKEUP)  
  
  
  SOFTWARE ENGINEERING [ICT 3123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                        Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Evaluate the strengths and limitations of the Concurrent Specialized Process Model when applied      (5)  
  to large-scale, distributed software development projects. How does this model work in comparison  
  to the Waterfall and Agile models in terms of flexibility, scalability, and risk management? Provide  
  specific examples to support your assessment.  
1B)               TechSol, a software development company, is developing a cloud-based customer management                  (3)  
  system (CMS) for a client. The project faces tight deadlines, and the team is working with an  
  unfamiliar technology stack. Additionally, the client requires the product to be deployed across  
  multiple regions, each with its own compliance requirements. The project manager has highlighted  
  several risks that may impact the success of the project. Based on this scenario, identify and  
  classify at least six potential risks according to the nature of their impact on the project. Explain how  
  the identified risks could jeopardize the success of the CMS project.  
1C)               Consider an online shopping system where customers can search for products, add them to a cart, (2)  
  and proceed to checkout. The thread-based testing identifies the following classes involved in the  
  checkout process:  
  
  Cart Class: Manages the items that the user has added to their shopping cart.  
  Payment Gateway Class: Handles the payment processing for the order.  
  Order Confirmation Class: Generates the order confirmation and updates the order status.  
  
  Describe how you would integrate and test these classes to ensure that the checkout functionality  
  works correctly when a user places an order. Provide at least two specific test cases for this thread.  
2A)               Create a class diagram for the management of flights and pilots scenario given below:                      (5)  
  An airline operates flights. Each airline has an ID. Each flight has an ID a departure airport and an  
  arrival airport: an airport as a unique identifier. Each flight has a pilot and a co-pilot, and it uses an  
  aircraft of a certain type; a flight has also a departure time and an arrival time. An airline owns a set  
  of aircrafts of different types. An aircraft can be in a working state, or it can be under repair. In a  
  particular moment an aircraft can be landed or airborne. A company has a set of pilots: each pilot  
  has an experience level: 1 is minimum, 3 is maximum. A type of aeroplane may need a particular  
  number of pilots, with a different role (e.g.: captain, co-pilot, navigator): there must be at least one  
  captain and one co-pilot, and a captain must have a level 3.  
2B)               Discuss the differences between elicitation and specification in requirements engineering. Highlight (3)  
  the key challenges encountered during elicitation and explain how these are addressed in the  
  specification process.  
2C)               Consider a software application consisting of five modules (A, B, C, D, and E) with the following          (2)  
  dependencies:  
  
  Module A calls Module B and Module C.  
  Page 1 of 3

Module B calls Module D.  
  Module C calls Module E.  
  Module D has no further dependencies.  
  Module E is a standalone module.  
  
  a) Determine the number of stubs required if you want to test Module A in isolation.  
  b) Identify the number of drivers needed to test Module D independently.  
  c) Provide the reason for the number of stubs and drivers considered in the above cases ( a & b) .  
3A)   You have been tasked with designing the software architecture for a large-scale e-commerce           (5)  
  platform. The platform needs to handle various functionalities, including managing customer orders,  
  processing payments, maintaining product catalogs, and providing real-time updates for inventory  
  and delivery statuses. The system also needs to ensure high availability, support for real-time data  
  processing, and scalability for millions of users.  
  Given the requirements of the e-commerce platform, evaluate which architectural style mentioned  
  below would be most suitable for this system: Data-centered architecture, Data-flow architecture,  
  Object-oriented architecture, or Layered architecture.  
  Justify your choice and explain the chosen architecture style.  
3B)   A mobile banking application requires users to log in using a 6-digit PIN. The system checks if the   (3)  
  PIN is valid based on specific rules:  
  
  The PIN must contain exactly 6 digits.  
  It must only contain numeric characters.  
  The PIN cannot be sequential (e.g., 123456 or 654321).  
  The output will either be "Valid PIN" or "Invalid PIN" based on these rules.  
  
  Using Black Box Equivalence Class Testing, define and describe the input and output equivalence  
  classes that should be tested for this scenario. For each class, provide an example test case, and  
  explain why it is important to consider that class.  
3C)   A leading healthcare organization is developing a new electronic health record (EHR) system aimed (2)  
  at enhancing patient care and streamlining administrative processes. The system is expected to  
  facilitate patient data management, allow secure access for healthcare professionals, support  
  clinical decision-making, and comply with stringent regulatory standards. Key stakeholders include  
  doctors, nurses, administrative staff, and patients. The organization emphasizes the importance of  
  data security, user satisfaction, system interoperability, and the ability to analyze large datasets for  
  insights into patient outcomes.  
  In the context of the EHR system classify the various quality attributes that are essential.  
4A)   Draw the control flow graph for the following function named find maximum and determine its           (5)  
  cyclomatic complexity:  
  int find-maximum(int i,int j, int k){  
  int max;  
  if(i>j) then  
  if(i>k) then  
  $$max=i;$$  
  $$else max=k;$$  
  else if(j>k)  
  $$max=j$$  
  $$else max=k;$$  
  return(max);  
  }  
4B)   Imagine you are part of an Agile team developing a new mobile app. After releasing an early           (3)  
  prototype to users, you receive feedback that certain features are confusing and not user-friendly.  
  How would you and your team use Agile principles to respond to this feedback in the next  
  development sprint, and what steps would you take to ensure that the final product meets user  
  expectations  
4C)   Identify the purpose of architectural patterns in software design.                                    (2)  
5A)   Draw UML sequence diagram for chat applications for exchanging messages in chat room.                 (5)  
5B)   Identify and explain the main activities involved in the requirement engineering process. How do      (3)  
  these activities ensure that the final product meets user needs?  
  Page 2 of 3

5C)   Identify four common risks associated with software development projects. For each risk, briefly   (2)  
  explain a possible mitigation strategy that could be employed to minimize its impact.  
  
  
  -----End-----
